claim: For distinct odd primes \(p<q\), the integer \(4pq\) is unitary half-Zumkeller if and only if \((p,q)\in\{(3,5),(3,7),(5,11),(7,13),(7,19)\}\). Equivalently, the only unitary half-Zumkeller integers of the form \(4pq\) are \(60,84,220,364,532\).
scientific limitations/integrity: The theorem is restricted to distinct odd primes \(p<q\) and dyadic exponent exactly two. The unbounded proof uses a symbolic inequality to reduce to \(p\in\{3,5,7\}\), followed by an exact finite enumeration of \(64\) sign triples per prime. A larger finite scan is regression evidence only. No claim is made for higher dyadic exponents, repeated odd-prime factors, or arbitrary three-prime-support integers. The earliest verified public source date is the dated OEIS A290467 entry, while primary MSC ownership is verified from Das’s article (MSC 11A25). The literature comparison has the ordinary residual risk of an obscure unindexed source.
title: Exact classification of unitary half-Zumkeller numbers of the form \(4pq\)
